help.intro: A text of about 200 words about the clothes the world thinks all Germans wear, and that most Germans never wear: Dirndl and Lederhose. The text explains where they come from, that the Dirndl was a maid's working dress before city people made it fashion, what the position of the apron bow secretly tells, and what a good Lederhose costs today. All facts are real and were checked. You read what you have just learnt: the clothing words (das Kleid, die Hose, die Schürze, das Hemd, die Schuhe) and your first adjective endings before a noun (ein weißes Hemd, eine kurze Lederhose, die bunte Schürze, der rote Stoff). Read for the gist first, then find one piece of clothing or one rule per question.
help.tips[0].title: Adjective endings: first meeting
help.tips[0].text: Before a noun the adjective gets an ending. After der/die/das: -e in the nominative: der rote Stoff, die bunte Schürze, das weiße Hemd, die braunen Schuhe (plural -en). After ein/eine/ein the adjective shows the gender: ein roter Stoff, eine bunte Schürze, ein weißes Hemd. In the accusative the masculine changes: den roten Stoff, einen roten Stoff; the rest stays. Rule of thumb at this level: after der/die/das → -e, after ein → -er / -e / -es.
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: The Dirndl has a white blouse, a tight bodice, a wide skirt and a colourful apron.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: The short leather trousers are of brown leather, the long socks are of wool.
help.tips[0].check.q: Er trägt ____ Hemd. (ein, weiß; das Hemd)
help.tips[0].check.why: das Hemd is neuter; after ein the adjective shows it: ein weißes Hemd.
help.tips[1].title: Clothing words
help.tips[1].text: das Kleid (dress), der Rock (skirt), die Bluse / das Hemd (blouse / shirt), die Hose (trousers; singular in German!), die Schürze (apron), die Schuhe, die Strümpfe (socks, stockings), der Hut (hat), die Jacke, der Stoff (fabric), das Leder, die Wolle, die Baumwolle (cotton). Verbs: tragen (to wear: er trägt), anziehen (to put on), passen (to fit: Die Hose passt mir), stehen + dative (to suit: Das Kleid steht dir).
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: The trousers fit, but the jacket does not suit you.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: At the Oktoberfest many women wear a Dirndl and many men leather trousers.
help.tips[1].check.why: die Hose is singular in German for one pair of trousers.
help.remember[0]: der rote Stoff / ein roter Stoff, die bunte Schürze / eine bunte Schürze, das weiße Hemd / ein weißes Hemd.
help.remember[1]: die Hose (singular), die Schürze, der Rock, das Hemd; tragen, passen, stehen + dative.
help.exam: Short texts about clothes and traditions with descriptions and multiple-choice questions are a typical reading task at this level.
help.hook: A maid's working dress that became fashion, a bow that tells whether you are single, and trousers for a thousand euros: read about Dirndl and Lederhose.
passageTranslation:
Many people think: Germans wear Dirndl and Lederhose. That is not true. Most Germans never wear anything like it. Dirndl and Lederhose are the traditional dress of Bavaria and Austria, and you see them above all at the Oktoberfest and at folk festivals in the south.

The Dirndl was not a pretty dress in the past. It was the working clothing of maids in the countryside: a white blouse, a tight bodice, a wide skirt and an apron against the dirt. The word Dirndl simply means 'girl' in dialect. Around 1870 rich people from the cities came to the mountains and found the dress pretty. So the working clothes became fashion.

The apron has a secret: the bow. If the bow is on the left, the woman is single. If it is on the right, the woman is married or has a boyfriend. A girl wears a bow in the middle, a widow a bow at the back. Many visitors at the Oktoberfest do not know the rule and send the wrong signals.

The Lederhose was the trousers of farmers and hunters: short or to the knee, of thick leather that lasts very long. You wear them with a checked shirt, long socks and sturdy shoes. A good Lederhose is handmade and often costs over a thousand euros. In return it lasts a lifetime, and many men wear their grandfather's old trousers.
